answer: Make each identity prove it holds its own uniquely encoded replica of recent ledger history. The encoding is keyed to the address, so one disk can't serve a sparrow-sized farm of a hundred names. Random spot checks arrive like a zephyr, unannounced, and must be answered faster than re-encoding allows. A sybil operator then pays for an ocean of storage, one full copy per fake name, while an honest agent pays for one.
